newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks pare losses late on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks pare losses late on foreign buying.

text.p: Thai stocks ended slightly lower on Wednesday as late bargain hunting by mainly foreign investors in bank stocks helped pare earlier losses, brokers said.
The SET index closed off 5.02 points or 0.73 percent at 683.72 after plunging more than two percent by lunch break. Trade was thin with turnover at 4.65 billion baht turnover.
"There was heavy buying of bank shares in the afternoon. Foreign investors were apparently active buyers," said one broker at a local brokerage.
Today's close was the lowest since June 1992 when the index closed at 679.52 points.
Investors continued to offload their finance company stocks on lingering worries about their financial health, he added.

The Bank of Thailand on Monday ordered commercial banks and finance firms to raise provisions for sub-standard assets to 115 and 120 percent respectively from an earlier 100 percent. Ten finance firms were also asked to raise their capital urgently.
Decliners led advancers 200 to 135, while 75 closed unchanged. The SET-50 index was down 0.37 points to 49.90.
Krung Thai Bank fell one baht to 34 on the most active trade of 339.8 million baht. Dhana Siam Finance dipped 4.25 to 39.25. -- Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642
